submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective, diffuse 'not running English text' dip rather than a detector of any one token set: this pole is the trough side of a layer-2 neuron (-min(gelu(pre),0), hard-capped at the gelu_new floor 0.170), it sits at 0.02-0.04 on ordinary English prose (pre-activation about -2) and reaches the cap only when the passage being read is not English prose - HTML/XML/JSX markup and attribute glue (' href', ' class', ' name', ' id', '="', '">', '></', '/' inside a URL path), text written wholly in another language or script ('東京は日本の首都です。', 'ona virüs ile mücadele', 'produceren'), the subword piece of an unusual proper noun ('Nairobi' -> 'airo'), and an instruction opener such as 'Please ...' that lifts the whole following clause. It is inactive on plain English declarative prose from its third token onward (measured peaks 0.00-0.03) and on a foreign-script or markup word dropped inside an otherwise English sentence (a CJK word at position 4 of an English sentence leaves the peak on the English baseline token at 0.034), while the second position of any sequence is elevated and only weakly predictable (0.03-0.17 depending on the opener), so label 'predicted inactive' only for running English prose or isolated foreign tokens and 'predicted active' for markup passages, whole non-English passages, subword pieces of unusual names and imperative openers.
